More precisely, I like watching the moment when a character stands at a crossroads and seeing what decision they make. Rather than flashy settings or vast worldbuilding, I began writing because I wanted to portray people wavering and growing within them.\r\nThe fantasy I write is not merely a display of power; it is a story that asks about the responsibility and price that come after gaining power. I focus on what is lost and what one tries to protect while growing stronger.\r\nMy goal is to create stories that make readers wonder at least once, “What would I have done in that situation?” I do not want to write novels that are consumed quickly, but ones in which a scene or a line of dialogue lingers for a long time.\r\nI am still an author in the process of learning, but my most important principle is to diligently build the story with every installment. I am working hard to write something I can take responsibility for until the end, even if it is not perfect, and something that makes readers look forward to the next chapter.\r\nIf this novel can briefly help someone forget reality at the end of their day, or leave even a small aftertaste in their heart, that is enough for me.\u007c\u007c\u007c
